rationale: The previous attempt to measure the exposure bound ran in a receipt whose exit code was 1: a configuration change in another test of the same file hit an election race ('remove 4: node is not the leader'), which also makes that receipt unusable for citation. The harness now retries configuration changes against the current leader, and a local run of all of its assurance cases passes, so the same measurement is requeued as a successor on the fixed harness.

experiment.revision_reason: Unrelated configuration changes in the same file are now retried against the current leader so an election racing the call cannot fail the run; the verification scenarios and the added bounded post-verification wait are unchanged.

scope.description: Two four-peer in-memory clusters (slowed timers and the repository's default in-memory timers) are each reduced to three voters plus one non-voter, the leader is disconnected from the two remaining voters while the non-voter stays wired, reachability is confirmed by direct AppendEntries attempts, VerifyLeader is called, and each case then waits, bounded by five lease timeouts, for the leader to stop reporting itself as leader.
assumptions: Cluster, transports and FSM are the repository's own MakeCluster, InmemTransport and MockFSM facilities; the demotion uses the public DemoteVoter API.
The leader remains connected to the non-voter and disconnected from the other voters for the whole case.
The step-down observation is bounded by five lease timeouts plus two seconds and records the lease timeout it used.

experiment.prefix: For each timer configuration: start a four-peer cluster, wait for a leader and apply one command; demote a follower so the configuration is three voters plus one non-voter; disconnect the leader from the other two voters in both directions; confirm reachability with direct AppendEntries attempts and emit the setup event with the voters, voter quorum, reachability results, identifiers and variant; call VerifyLeader and emit the result event; then wait, bounded by five lease timeouts, until the leader no longer reports itself as leader and emit the lease-bound event with the lease timeout, the elapsed wait and the final state.
experiment.requirement: Leader verification must not report success unless a voter quorum of the configuration in force has acknowledged, and the isolated leader must stop reporting itself as leader within a bounded interval after losing that quorum.
experiment.responsibility: Raft itself: verifyLeader chooses which peers' acknowledgements count, and checkLeaderLease decides when the leader steps down.

comparisons.description: With slowed timers, verification fails while only a non-voter can acknowledge.
With default timers, verification fails while only a non-voter can acknowledge.
With default timers the isolated leader stops reporting itself as leader within the bounded wait.
